resources.kind_desc.skill: How the AI does a job
resources.kind_how.agent: Upload its directory, or have it come from the resource repository
resources.kind_how.knowledge: No text is uploaded: it points at a directory of a Git repository
resources.kind_how.mcp: How to connect and where, and the secrets each person provides
resources.kind_how.skill: A directory: SKILL.md with references and scripts. The AI loads it by its description
resources.kind_how.workflow: Delivered as a slash command; as a skill in tools without slash commands
resources.lead: Who gets a resource and how — its scope, stages and install policy — takes effect as soon as you save. New content arrives as a draft and reaches people only when it is published. Skills, workflows and agents are best kept in a Git resource repository and reviewed there; uploading on the web is the fallback.
resources.narrow.body: With the scope set to {{scope}}, {{people}} people on {{devices}} computers lose it at their next sync.
resources.narrow.title: Narrow the scope?
resources.new.code_hint: The same code as the directory in the archive. Cannot change once published.
resources.new.created: Created as a draft; publish it to hand it out
resources.new.lead: Choose the kind first: each comes in differently
resources.new.repo_first: Skills, workflows and agents are best committed to the resource repository, where the platform imports them as drafts: {{cli}} skill new <code> makes the skeleton and {{cli}} check runs the same checks on your computer.
resources.new.title: New resource
resources.new.upload_hint: Name, stages and the rest come from the files in the archive and can be changed afterwards.
resources.rollback.body: v{{next}} is published with the content of v{{version}}; people get it at their next sync.
resources.rollback.note_ph: e.g. The newest version breaks projects without a template
resources.rollback.title: Roll back to v{{version}}?
resources.upload.desc: A zip or tar archive of the resource's directory; it is checked as soon as it arrives
resources.upload.done: Uploaded and checked; it is a draft until published
resources.upload.title: Upload a new version
resources.upload.too_big: The archive is larger than this server accepts.
resources.versions.diff_none: The draft has the same files as the live version.
resources.versions.hint: Rolling back never deletes history; it publishes an old version's content again as a new version. On a computer, {{cli}} status {{code}} --diff compares versions.
resources.versions.pending: There is new content that is not published yet. People still get v{{version}}.
resources.versions.rolled_back: Rolled back: v{{version}} has the content of v{{from}}
resources.via.native: Native: written into the MCP configuration
resources.via.on_demand: On demand: delivered as a skill
resources.waive.hint: Kept in the audit log. It stops applying as soon as that line changes.
resources.waive.reason: Why this is not a real problem
resources.waive.reason_ph: e.g. A documented example value, not a real password
resources.waive.title: Mark as a false alarm
settings.lead: Everything the setup wizard asked can be changed here. Every change is recorded in the audit log.
settings.mail.hint: TLS is for port 465; with STARTTLS the server must offer it, or nothing is sent.
settings.mail.password_set: Saved; type a new one to replace it
settings.mail.port_bad: The port is a number from 1 to 65535.
settings.mail.send_desc: Invitations, review requests and replies to feedback. Off, people only see notifications in the console.
settings.mail.test_hint: Uses the saved settings. If it fails, the mail server's answer is shown here.
settings.mail.test_save_first: Save first: the test uses the saved settings
settings.mail.test_sent: The mail server accepted it; check the inbox of {{to}}
settings.mail.title: Mail
settings.modules.ask_hint: You can turn it off again at any time.
settings.modules.hint: Turning a module off keeps its data; turning it back on picks up where it left off.
settings.modules.locked: The deployment turned it off; it cannot be turned on here.
settings.modules.none: This server was built without optional modules.
settings.modules.off: {{name}} is off; its data is kept
settings.modules.title: Optional modules
settings.org.hint: Shown on the sign-in page and in mail.
settings.org.name: Name
settings.org.title: Organisation
settings.sources.added: Added {{name}}; the first pull has started
settings.sources.dir_note: Where its configuration file is; empty for the root
settings.sources.failed_desc: Pull {{when}} failed: {{why}}. Last good pull {{last}}; its resources stay as they were.
settings.sources.failed_never: Pull {{when}} failed: {{why}}. Nothing has been imported yet.
settings.sources.hint: The repository is where the content lives. New content comes in as drafts; people decide whether to publish it, for which product and at which stages. When two repositories have the same code, the one higher up wins.
settings.sources.name: Name
settings.sources.none: No resource repository yet. Resources can still be added on the resources page, but keeping skills, workflows and agents in Git gets them reviewed like code.
settings.sources.ok_desc_one: Pulled {{when}} · {{resources}} resource, {{imported}} changed and imported as drafts
settings.sources.ok_desc_other: Pulled {{when}} · {{resources}} resources, {{imported}} changed and imported as drafts
settings.sources.remove_ask: Imported resources keep their versions; they just get no new drafts.
settings.sources.removed: Stopped importing from {{name}}; resources already imported stay as they are
settings.sources.title: Resource repositories
settings.sources.token_hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. A token that can only read is enough.
settings.sources.token_set: Saved; type a new one to replace it
settings.sources.url_bad: Use an https:// or ssh address (ssh://… or git@host:path).
settings.sources.url_hint: An https or ssh Git address.
setup.admin.done: The administrator {{name}} ({{username}}) is created and signed in.
setup.admin.error.password: The password needs at least {{min}} characters.
setup.admin.error.token: This is not the setup token. Copy it again from the server log.
setup.admin.error.token_empty: Enter the setup token from the server log.
setup.admin.error.username: Use 2 to 32 lower-case letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter or a digit.
setup.admin.exists: The administrator was created already. Sign in with that account to finish the setup.
setup.admin.lead: This is the platform's first start. Enter the setup token from the server log, then create a local administrator account: it is the way in when an identity provider has trouble.
setup.admin.password.hint: Only a hash is stored. If it is forgotten, run {{cmd}} on the server.
setup.admin.token.hint: Printed in the server log on first start. It works once and expires when setup is finished. With Docker, run {{cmd}} to see it.
setup.methods.error.last: At least one sign-in method has to stay on.
setup.methods.error.none: Pick at least one way to sign in.
setup.methods.gitlab.desc: Self-hosted or gitlab.com, with an OAuth application
setup.methods.gitlab.name: GitLab
setup.methods.later: You can set the sign-in methods up later in Platform settings.
setup.methods.lead: Choose how people sign in. Pick several if you like; change them later in Users & sign-in.
setup.methods.local.desc: The administrator invites people; they set a password the first time
setup.methods.oidc.desc: Fill in the issuer address, the client ID and the client secret
setup.methods.oidc.name: Company SSO
setup.methods.secret.hint: Encrypted when saved; nobody can read it back.
setup.privacy.empty.title: No optional modules
setup.privacy.empty.why: This server was built without optional modules, so nothing is collected and there is nothing to turn on.
setup.privacy.hint: All off by default. Change them later in Platform settings; every change is audited.
setup.privacy.lead: Usage insights collect metadata only (counts, outcomes, durations, which resource was used), never questions, code, call arguments or results.
setup.privacy.locked: Turned off by the deployment; it cannot be turned on here.
setup.product.code.hint: The first word of its commands; it cannot be changed later
setup.product.error.code: Lower-case letters and digits, words joined by hyphens, at least 2 characters.
setup.product.error.name: Give the product a name.
setup.product.error.reserved: This is a command name or reserved; choose another code.
setup.product.lead: Products decide who can see which resources. Create one now and the rest later.
setup.product.name: Name
setup.product.owner.hint: Owners review requests to join and manage the product's resources.
setup.product.skip: Leave the name and the code empty to finish without a product.
setup.repo.error.url: An https:// or ssh address of a Git repository.
setup.repo.hint: By default the platform pulls every 10 minutes. Changed resources come in as drafts; publishing is still decided by people.
setup.repo.lead: The resource repository is a plain Git repository holding skills, workflows, agents and the rest as files; the platform only reads it. You can skip this and register resources on the web later.

shell.nav.label: Main navigation
shell.side.label: Sidebar
tools.base1.title: Everything can be previewed before it is written
tools.base2.title: Every write is in the manifest; one command removes it all
tools.base3.desc: Only entries with the product's prefix, and only with the person's consent
tools.base3.title: Global settings are never changed silently
tools.cli.min_hint: Older ones cannot sync and are told to upgrade. At least {{floor}}.
tools.cli.spread_none: No computer has reported its version yet.
tools.cli.title: Command-line versions
tools.disabled: {{tool}} is off: nothing more is written into it, and what was written is cleaned up at each computer's next sync
tools.enabled: {{tool}} is on: resources are written into it from each computer's next sync
tools.fallback.1.then: Workflows are delivered as skills with the same name; the description says how to start them
tools.fallback.1.when: The tool has no slash commands
tools.fallback.2.then: Agents are delivered as skills: an entry point plus the skills they bring
tools.fallback.3.then: A skill explains the server and the calls go through {{cli}} mcp call
tools.fallback.3.when: The tool cannot load MCP servers on demand
tools.fallback.4.then: No sessions or friction are collected; only calls through the platform are recorded
tools.fallback.4.when: The tool has no hooks, or the person did not agree to them
tools.fallback.5.then: Nothing is written; it reports the error. It never treats the file as empty
tools.fallback.5.when: The adapter cannot read an existing configuration file
tools.fallback.title: Fallback rules
tools.lead: Each AI tool has an adapter profile: where resources are written, in which format, and what happens when the tool lacks something. A tool with a similar structure needs only a new profile, no new code.
tools.none: This server has no tool adapters.
tools.note: The landing places come from each adapter's built-in profile and were checked against the tool version shown. A tool that is not checked yet gets nothing written, whatever its switch says. A computer can turn a tool off for itself, but not turn on one that is off here.
tools.verified_title: The landing places were checked against version {{version}} of the tool
ui.aitip.label: Ask the AI
ui.copy_failed: Could not copy: the browser does not let this page use the clipboard. Select the text and copy it by hand.
ui.fail.forbidden: You are not allowed to do this. If you need to, ask a platform administrator.
ui.fail.network: Cannot reach the server. Check the network and try again.
ui.fail.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
ui.fail.server: The server could not do this (HTTP {{status}}). Try again shortly; if it keeps happening, tell your platform administrator.
ui.fail.stale: Someone changed this in the meantime. It has been reloaded; look at it again and repeat your change.
ui.load.denied.title: Not allowed to see this
ui.load.denied.why: The server refused: your account may not see this. Ask a product owner or a platform administrator if you need access.
ui.load.failed.title: This did not load
ui.load.failed.why: The server did not answer properly. Try again later; if it keeps happening, tell a platform administrator.
ui.load.offline.title: Cannot reach the server
ui.load.offline.why: Check the network, or make sure the server is running, then try again.
ui.selftip.label: Only you
users.denied.title: For platform administrators
users.denied.why: Accounts, invitations and sign-in methods are managed by platform administrators. Product owners decide on requests to join in Products & members.
users.done.disable: Disabled {{name}}: web, command-line and access tokens stop working now; platform resources leave their computers at the next sync.
users.done.unadmin: {{name}} is no longer a platform administrator (audited).
users.empty.title: No accounts
users.empty.why: Accounts appear here when people sign in or accept an invitation.
users.error.last_admin: The platform needs at least one administrator.
users.foot: At least one platform administrator always remains. The local administrator is the account created at setup, the way in when an identity provider is down. There are no default passwords: local accounts set theirs through the one-time link in their invitation.
users.invite.error.empty: Enter at least one e-mail address.
users.invite.error.exists: One of these addresses already has an account.
users.invite.hint: They get a one-time link valid for seven days. People who sign in with SSO or GitLab need no invitation; they apply the first time they sign in.
users.invite.links.hint: Anyone with a link can create that account, so send it only to the person it is for. Set up mail in Platform settings to send them automatically.
users.invite.links.lead: Mail is not set up on this server, so nothing was sent. Pass each link on yourself; this is the only time they are shown.
users.invite.links.title: Send these links yourself
users.invite.products.none: No products yet. People can ask to join products after signing in.
users.invite.title: Invite colleagues
users.invites.empty.title: No invitations waiting
users.invites.empty.why: Invite colleagues who will use a local account. People who sign in with SSO or GitLab need no invitation.
users.invites.foot: Each link works once and for seven days. Withdrawing one stops it at once.
users.invites.revoked: Withdrawn: the link for {{email}} no longer works.
users.lead: People sign in with company SSO, GitLab or a local account, and the first time they ask for products and pick their job themselves. Here you decide on requests, change who administers the platform and disable accounts.
users.methods.error.changed: Someone changed the sign-in methods meanwhile. Close this and open it again.
users.methods.error.last: At least one sign-in method has to stay on.
users.methods.more: Add a method or change its addresses in
users.methods.secret.hint: Only in the browser; an AI tool cannot fill it in.
users.methods.secret.saved: <saved; enter a new value to replace it>
users.methods.title: Sign-in methods
users.reject.error.empty: Write why, so they know what to change.
users.reject.reason.placeholder: Such as: check with your team lead which product to join first
users.reject.title: Decline the request
users.requests.approved: Approved: {{name}} gets the resources of {{product}} from their next sign-in.
users.requests.empty.title: No requests waiting
users.requests.empty.why: When someone signs in with SSO or GitLab for the first time and asks to join a product, the request shows up here.
users.requests.error.decided: Someone decided on this request already. Reload to see the result.
users.requests.foot: A product's owners can also decide on its requests in Products & members. Declining needs a reason, and the person is told.
